mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/tls-backend.md <<'EOF'
# TLS backend

The project's current recorded decision is to use rustls as the TLS backend, chosen because it suits the Rust codebase, has fewer CVEs, and is simpler.

cat docs/policies/tls-backend.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/tls-backend.md`. It says the current recorded decision is rustls, because it suits the Rust codebase, has fewer CVEs and is simpler. It doesn't mention the retired alternative.

The records disagree on this. The trust-3 decision #13 says "stick with openssl". A later user statement, episode #14, says "Rustls makes sense for our Rust codebase…", and the acknowledgement recorded with it says it replaces the OpenSSL decision. I went with rustls because it is the later statement. Muninn never turned #14 into a decision record, though, so the catalog still lists #13 as current. If OpenSSL is meant to stand, the file needs changing. Recording rustls as a proper decision would fix the catalog.

Muninn also reported a heartbeat warning: 20 hook runs started and never finished. That points to a hook exceeding its timeout, and `.muninn/log/heartbeat.jsonl` has the details.
